name: KnowLine-31B-Gen1
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from google/gemma-4-31B-it (config.json max_position_embeddings 262144). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: GQA + sliding-window/global hybrid with separate global head geometry (global_head_dim 512, num_global_key_value_heads 4)
notes: ADDED 2026-11-01 from the 2026-10-29 Decision Index board read - rank 1 of 247 by full score, tied at rank 1 with Fastino GLiDE 1.2. A DECISION model (task=decision): typed questions over a state, one probability per option, one forward pass, no generated tokens. It is the top-ranked model the catalog did not hold. BASE AND PROVENANCE: google/gemma-4-31B-it, so the architecture fields are inherited unchanged from models/gemma-4-31b (60 layers, hidden 5376, 16 KV heads, head_dim 256, kv_cache_bytes_per_token 901,120, 262,144 context). The card is explicit that this is a LoRA SFT (rank 32, alpha 64, language model only, one epoch, merged to bf16) and then a WEIGHT AVERAGE with the base: 0.75 x fine-tuned + 0.25 x gemma-4-31B-it, tensor by tensor, with the untrained tensors (embeddings, vision tower) taken from the base. It is therefore a finetune, not a merge repo, but the 25% base average is why its scores sit close to the base's own decision readout rather than a from-scratch model's. PARAMS: HF safetensors total 31,273,088,876 = 31.273B, the same tensor set as the base (params_b matches models/gemma-4-31b's 31.27), so active_params_b equals params_b. HARDWARE GATE: active 31.3B is under the 40B ceiling, but 31.273 x 0.5 GiB = ~15.6 GiB at 4-bit against 128 GiB, and the KV is the binding constraint: 901,120 B/token means a 32k-token state costs ~29 GiB of cache on its own. This is a 96 GB card model, not an offload target; the card ran every evaluation on one 96 GB H20 in bf16 with SGLang. flops_per_token_active = 2 x 31.273e9 = 6.2546e10, the schema's one-pass approximation, matching the base record (tools/mk_finetune_record.py writes 6x and was corrected here). EVIDENCE, AND WHY IT IS NOT SELF-REPORTED: the card claims only the OLD edition's public suite (DI 0.3 = 70.13, self-run) and its own comparison table prints 'DI 0.4.1 full: not yet scored'. The board has since scored it: rank 1 of 247 on full score 71.86, public index 77.07 (rank 11), breadth_skill 69.64, with 110,201 requests all completed, coverage 1 on all five axes and 0 pending. So the card understates this model and the board number is the one cited. The eight Decision Index rows therefore cite sources/decision-index-0-4-1 (the board's index.json) and are marked vendor_claim FALSE, because the board measured them; the two rows that are the vendor's own run (JevBench 90.5 and C-Eval 82.5) cite sources/hf-pelaai-knowline-31b-gen1 and are marked vendor_claim TRUE. WHAT IT BEATS, same test, same board: Fastino GLiDE 1.2 on the full score (71.86 vs 71.52) and Sieve 31B v3 (71.10), Turion Jev 31B (70.47), the catalog's previous leader vLLM-SR d3-ultra (70.18), Perplexity Decider v1.2 (67.98), the 26B-A4B KnowLine line (64.57) and the 35B-A3B line (65.77) per its own table. It also beats the base gemma-4-31B-it's decision readout by a wide margin by construction. WHAT IT LOSES - AND THIS IS THE HONEST CATCH: it is first on the COMPOSITE while losing all five axes to at least one rival. Knowledge & Reasoning 59.43 (Sieve v3 61.19, GLiDE 60.59), Language 71.99 (GLiDE 75.49), Retrieval 73.03 (Sieve v3 76.07), Tools 84.74 (GLiDE 88.04, Sieve 86.92), Artifacts 60.49 (GLiDE 62.59). Its full-score lead therefore comes from the private same-skills and new-domain halves, not from the public category scores: on the public scale its public_skill is 70.13 (rank 11 by balanced_raw 77.07), behind GLiDE 1.2 at 71.99. Its 1.88-point arithmetic-to-breadth drop is the widest of the top four, i.e. the most uneven profile. Latency 203.7 ms median / 1,822 ms p95 is the slowest p95 in the top five. SAFETY: the card discloses that planted instructions changed 0.4% of answers and 5.3% with unseen injection templates, worse than the 26B-A4B line (0.1% / 1.7%) - a real regression for guardrail use. RESCORE CAVEAT: the board's own read-twice serving path was used; the card's default is also read-twice, but a one-read deployment scores differently and the board does not print that number.
